title: Elizabeth I & the Armada Adventure
welcome_lead: It's 1588 and a giant Spanish fleet is heading for England. Stand with Queen Elizabeth I as the Armada approaches. ⛵
meta_desc: Elizabeth I Adventure — a KS3 History walkthrough of the Spanish Armada 1588 and the Elizabethan age.
final_note: You met Elizabeth I, learned why Spain attacked, and saw how storms and small English ships saved England.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Elizabeth I became queen in 1558 aged 25. She was Protestant; Spain was Catholic.

Spain ruled a huge empire and was the most powerful country in Europe. King Philip II of Spain had even been married to Elizabeth's sister Mary I.

Philip wanted to make England Catholic again — by force. ⚔️

In 1588, Philip II sent the Spanish Armada — about 130 ships — to pick up an invasion army from the Netherlands and land it in England.

The English fleet was smaller but faster. Sailors like Francis Drake and Lord Howard waited in the Channel.

Elizabeth rode to Tilbury and told her troops: 'I have the body of a weak and feeble woman, but the heart and stomach of a king.' 👑

While the Armada anchored at Calais, the English sent in fireships at night. The Spanish panicked and cut their anchors.

The next day at the Battle of Gravelines, English guns drove the Armada into the North Sea. Storms then smashed ships on the coasts of Scotland and Ireland.

Only about half the Spanish ships made it home. England had been saved — and Elizabeth's reputation soared. 🌊

mcqs.q: What were the long-term effects of the Black Death?
options: Labour shortages strengthened peasants' bargaining power, weakened serfdom in England, contributed to the Peasants' Revolt, and reshaped religious authority.
The Black Death was caused by witches and was stopped by burning them.
Weimar was unstable because the Kaiser was still secretly in charge.
The Black Death wiped out medieval society and ended the Middle Ages overnight.
